## Goal (tracer-bullet vertical slice)

Ship the first end-to-end music slice: the menu/attract ambient track ("Star Drift", Lydian) played through the existing shared AudioContext, driven by a minimal music state machine, with the autoplay/gesture guard and an independent music volume control.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.
- [ ] Music volume and mute are independent of SFX and persisted in the settings record.
- [ ] The state machine enters and leaves the menu/attract state only at a bar boundary of the shared beat clock.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stem looping, the gesture guard, independent volume routing and the menu/attract transition; all playback degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext.

- [ ] Covers parent AC5: **Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.

## Minimal implementation

1. Bake the "Star Drift" ambient stem via the ToneForge pipeline and add it to the cue/stem manifest (smallest slice of the stem pipeline).
2. Add src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (facade) and a minimal src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts with the menu/attract state.
3. Wire gesture-driven start/resume through MenuScene using the shared AudioContext.
4. Extend SettingsRecord with musicVolume/musicMuted and route them independently of SFX.
5. Add unit tests for each acceptance criterion.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by Music contract mapping and traceability guard (AH-0MVMH2OPY001X6M3), which is itself blocked by the chapter docs item (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W).
- Reuses the shared AudioContext and provider seam in src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts.

## Risky assumption

Baked stems (not runtime synthesis) are the delivery mechanism, consistent with the shipped ToneForge pipeline; recorded as an assumption in the parent item's plan.

**Key Files:**
- src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (new)
- src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts (new)
- src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts (shared AudioContext/provider seam to reuse)
- src/scenes/MenuScene.ts (gesture + menu/attract wiring)
- src/core/settingsStore.ts (music volume/mute)
- audio/toneforge/manifest.json (stem entry)
- scripts/build-audio.sh (bake pipeline)

data.description:
# We need an outer loop (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC)

## Objective

**User story (producer).** As the producer, I want the region/home-world proposal
plus **two genuinely different** outer-loop candidates, each written up as a
decision-ready outline on the same footing, so that I can choose one and have it
written into the Game Design Document (GDD) with confidence.

**User story (player).** As a player, I want something to carry forward between
runs — a long-term goal and a sense that my play changes the world — so that
losing a run does not mean losing all progress, and so that beating the final
boss is a milestone on the way to winning rather than the end of everything.

## Users

- **Producer / designer (primary).** Chooses one of three outlined loops and owns
  the GDD write-up; needs comparable, honest outlines and a defensible ranking.
- **Player (arcade / bullet-hell fan).** Needs a reason to return after a lost
  run and a goal beyond a high score; wants progress that survives failure.
- **Developer / agent implementing the loop later.** Needs each outline to name
  the systems, seams and gym coverage so the chosen loop can be planned without
  re-deriving the design.

## Problem statement

The game has a strong **inner loop** (flying, dodging formations, destroying
enemies) and a functioning **middle loop** (per-run ship upgrading through
minerals → hold-full power-up choices → levelled weapons), but **no outer loop**:
nothing persists between runs except a leaderboard score, player settings and a
single run checkpoint. A death ends the run outright (GDD §4.6: "There is no
continue mechanic. Game over is final"), so long-term engagement rests entirely
on score chasing. The fiction ("pilot a resistance ship through a digital
underworld ruled by rogue AI") implies a war to be won, but the game currently
has no structure that represents winning it.

The producer has proposed one candidate outer loop (contested regions with a
home world to find and defend) and asked for **two other candidates** to be
brainstormed and outlined, after which the producer chooses one for the GDD.

## Deliverable

A single design-exploration document — `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — built
to the same standard as the existing research catalogues
(`docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`):
selected candidates written up per-concept, a "considered but not selected"
section, and a selection recommendation. It is a **design document only**: no
gameplay code, no persistence schema changes and no new scenes are implemented
in this item.

The producer's choice is then written into the GDD as a follow-on work item; this
item ends at the candidate document, the comparison and the recommendation.

## Loop tiers used by the document

| Tier | Timescale | Definition in this game | Exists today? |
|------|-----------|-------------------------|---------------|
| **Inner** | Seconds | Flying, dodging, destroying enemies and formations within a wave | Yes (GDD §2.3–2.6) |
| **Middle** | Minutes (a run) | Ship upgrading: minerals → hold-full power-up/weapon choices, levelled effects, extra lives | Yes (GDD §4.4, §4.6) |
| **Outer** | Hours (a campaign / a season) | What the player carries **between** runs and what they are ultimately trying to achieve | **No** |

## Candidate A — Contested Regions / Home World (producer's proposal)

Recorded as proposed, not redesigned. Its outline must preserve every named
mechanic:

- Space is divided into **regions**; each region has an **AI aggression level**.
- The ship can **warp a limited distance** to adjacent regions.
- The goal is to find a region with **zero aggression** containing a **planet
  that can become home to the humans**.
- Having found it, the player must **defend all adjacent regions** against
  attack by aggressive AI.
- The player may leave their **fully upgraded ship** in a region with an **AI
  automated pilot** that defends that region.
- The player then returns home and **collects another ship with no upgrades**,
  and must go out again to make it strong enough to be left guarding another
  region.
- **Factional AI warfare** changes region strength over time: warring AI
  factions fight over a region and the winner leaves a stronger force there.
- **Win condition:** all regions have successfully defended against a massive AI
  onslaught, at which point the home world is safe and the game is won.

The outline must state its **minimal first slice** (the smallest version that
proves the loop is fun), because the full proposal is the largest of the three.

## Candidate B — Salvage Fleet (proposed direction, resource-persistent meta)

A **roguelite meta-progression** outer loop that leaves the map alone and
persists **player power** instead.

- Between runs the player spends **banked salvage** (minerals and mini-boss AI
  cores extracted at the existing checkpoint moments) in a persistent **hangar**
  to unlock hulls, starting weapons and permanent modifiers.
- Each run is a **deployment** flown in one chosen hull; losing the run forfeits
  that run's unbanked salvage but never the hangar.
- The outer goal is to assemble a fleet strong enough for a final assault run at
  maximum threat.
- Progression axis: **build/economy** (what the player owns), not territory.

## Candidate C — Signal Decode (proposed direction, knowledge-persistent meta)

A **campaign-mutating** outer loop where the thing that persists is
**information**.

- Mini-bosses and the boss drop **data fragments** that assemble a persistent
  codex revealing the origin of the AI and the "hellscape" it generates.
- Codex knowledge **mutates and unlocks the campaign** (new enemy behaviours,
  hellscape modifiers, shortcuts), and the final confrontation only becomes
  winnable once the core's rules have been decoded — the boss's phases are the
  codex's payoff.
- Progression axis: **knowledge and campaign variation**, not territory or
  currency.

## Required outline structure (every candidate)

1. **Fantasy / pitch** — one paragraph, in the game's fiction.
2. **Loop structure** — moment-to-moment → run → meta, with an explicit
   statement of *what carries between runs*.
3. **States** — win, lose, partial progress and what a bad run still advances.
4. **New systems** required (named, with rough size).
5. **Reuse of existing systems** — checkpoint (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`),
   minerals/power-up levels, `Leaderboard`, difficulty curves
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`), mini-boss rewards, bot/attract mode.
6. **Persistence and save model** — a sketch `localStorage` payload under
   §6.6 rules (defensive parse, no backend) with migration note.
7. **Session shape** — target run length and hours-to-win.
8. **UI / scene surface** — which new screens or menu entries are needed.
9. **Gym testability and the bot** — how its gameplay additions can be exercised
   in a gym (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity rule) and how attract mode can complete
   or avoid stalling on the outer loop.
10. **Pillar impact** — which current GDD pillars it changes (e.g. "no continue,
    game over is final", the single final boss), stated explicitly.
11. **Effort and risk** — sized honestly, with the failure modes that would make
    the loop unfun.
12. **Minimal first slice** — the smallest shippable version.

A **comparison table** then ranks all candidates on: fit with the existing
pilots-in-a-digital-hell fiction, reuse of shipped systems, new-system cost,
persistence complexity, session length fit, legibility of progress to the player,
gym/bot testability, and risk of trivialising or gutting the shipped campaign —
followed by an explicit **recommendation with rationale** and why the others rank
lower. A "Considered but not selected" section records further ideas (e.g. an
arcade-style tiered mutator ladder, a pure daily-seed challenge ladder) with a
one-line deferral reason each.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Deliverable exists and frames the problem.** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
   exists, opens with the inner/middle/outer tier definitions above and the
   comparison criteria, and states that it is design-only.
2. **Candidate A is complete and faithful.** Candidate A is written up with all
   twelve required sections and preserves every mechanic listed in *Candidate A*
   above (regions, limited warp, per-region aggression, zero-aggression home
   region with a habitable planet, defence of adjacent regions, autonomous-pilot
   ship hand-off, unupgraded replacement ship, faction warfare, all-regions-held
   win). No proposed mechanic is silently dropped, altered or merged.
3. **Two additional candidates, materially distinct.** Candidates B and C each
   carry all twelve required sections and each names *what persists between
   runs* differently from Candidate A and from each other; each is justified
   against at least one named design pillar or fiction element.
4. **Decision-ready comparison.** The document contains a comparison table across
   the agreed criteria, an explicit recommendation with rationale, and a ranked
   justification for why the two non-recommended candidates rank lower.
5. **Alternatives recorded.** A "Considered but not selected" section lists at
   least two further outer-loop ideas with a one-line deferral reason each.
6. **Docs guard test.** A vitest docs-guard test (convention:
   `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`) asserts the document exists,
   contains the tier definitions, the comparison table and, for each of the three
   candidates, the twelve required section headings — so the deliverable cannot
   silently regress. It passes in the changed-scope test gate.
7. **Cross-linked, not orphaned.** The new document is cross-linked from the GDD
   future-scope section (§8) and from where the other design catalogues are
   referenced in `README.md`; every added link resolves to a file or anchor that
   exists.
8. **Producer decision is staged, not pre-empted.** The document ends with a
   "Producer decision record" section (candidate | decision | date | notes) left
   pending, plus a note that the chosen loop's GDD write-up is a follow-on work
   item. No GDD gameplay text for the chosen loop is written in this item.
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `README.md`, and the GDD cross-links.
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Design only.** No gameplay, persistence-schema or scene implementation in
  this item; each candidate is marked "design only, not scheduled".
- **No backend.** All persistence must fit the existing `localStorage` model
  (GDD §6.6) with defensive parsing, as the leaderboard and checkpoint do.
- **Engine policy.** Candidates must not require a new engine or editor-driven
  content (GDD §6.1: code-first, Phaser).
- **Pillars are explicit, not accidental.** A candidate may propose changing an
  existing pillar (e.g. "no continue", the single final boss) but must say so in
  its *Pillar impact* section with a rationale and a cost.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Any gameplay element a candidate proposes must be
  exercisable in a gym scene, and the outline must say how (AGENTS.md parity
  rule, `src/scenes/gym/`, `GymFormationScene`).
- **Attract mode must not stall.** The demo bot must be able to traverse or skip
  any new outer-loop UI (§2.1 attract/demo mode).
- **Scope discipline.** Opportunities discovered mid-draft become linked work
  items, not added scope.
- **Write location and language.** Deliverable lives in `docs/` (no planning
  documents in the repo root); UK English and Markdown throughout.
- **Session shape must be stated.** Each candidate names its target run length
  and its hours-to-win, so the producer can compare commitment.

## Existing state

- **Inner/middle loops shipped:** 10-level campaign, 100 waves, 10 mini-bosses,
  one multi-phase final boss (GDD §3, §4.6); minerals and hold-full power-up
  choices are the middle loop's currency (§4.4); difficulty scaling is data-driven
  (`src/core/levelScaling.ts`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`).
- **Persistence today:** `ai_hell_leaderboard` (top-10 scores), `ai_hell_settings`,
  `ai_hell_checkpoint` (auto-written at each mini-boss defeat and offering
  "Continue — Level N"), `ai_hell_lastSession` (GDD §6.6).
- **No meta layer:** no persistent currency, unlock tree, map/region structure or
  cross-run progression of any kind. Game over is final (GDD §4.6).
- **Design-document precedent:** `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` and
  `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` are the established pattern for
  candidate-selection research, each with a sibling docs-guard test
  (`src/classicEnemyResearchDocs.test.ts`,
  `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`).

## Desired change

The repo gains one decision-ready design document describing three outer-loop
candidates on equal footing, with a comparison, a recommendation, deferral
reasons for rejected ideas and a docs guard that keeps the document honest — so
the producer can choose one loop with full information and the GDD write-up can
start immediately afterwards.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — **new**; the deliverable (candidate outlines,
  comparison, recommendation, deferrals, producer decision record).
- `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` — **new**; docs guard asserting the
  document's required sections and per-candidate headings, following the
  `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts` convention.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **edit**; §8 Future Scope cross-link to the new
  document (no gameplay text for a candidate in this item).
- `README.md` — **edit**; add the new document where the other design catalogues
  are referenced.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — **reference only**; the existing between-level
  persistence seam any outer loop will build on.
- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts`, `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` —
  **reference only**, to ground each candidate's reuse claims.

## Out of scope

- Implementing any candidate's systems (map, currency, codex, hangar, regions).
- Writing the chosen loop into the GDD as playable specification (follow-on item).
- Balancing or tuning anything that already ships.
- CHANGELOG.md (managed by the release pipeline).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — deliverable shape.** "Brainstorm two other possible outer loops
  and write an outline for each" is read as a design-exploration deliverable in
  `docs/`, matching the existing research-catalogue precedent, with Candidate A
  (the producer's proposal) included so the two alternatives are compared fairly.
- **Assumption — no implementation.** "I will choose one to be written up in the
  GDD" means the GDD write-up is the *next* item, so this item stops at the
  decision-ready document.
- **Risk — pillar conflict.** Every attractive outer loop tends to break "game
  over is final" or the single-final-boss structure; mitigated by the mandatory
  *Pillar impact* section and by stating each candidate's cost explicitly.
- **Risk — Candidate A is very large** (region graph, autonomous pilots, faction
  simulation). Mitigated by requiring a *Minimal first slice* per candidate.
- **Risk — scope creep into implementation** while drafting. Mitigated by the
  design-only constraint and by filing discovered opportunities as linked work
  items.
- **Risk — over-specified docs guard.** The guard asserts headings and required
  terms only, never prose wording, so the document stays editable.
- **Risk — comparison feels arbitrary.** Mitigated by publishing the criteria in
  the document before the candidates (AC1) and ranking against each.

## Related work

- **Game Design Document for AI_Hell (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — the living GDD this
  document feeds; §2.3–2.6 (inner loop), §4.4/§4.6 (middle loop, level
  progression), §5–§6 (leaderboard, save data), §8 (future scope).
- **Checkpoint save/resume (AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51)** — the existing persistence
  precedent the outer loop extends or replaces.
- **New enemies from classic arcade games (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52)** and
  **New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4)** —
  the candidate-selection research pattern this document follows.
- **Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry
  (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4)** — the bot that must remain able to traverse any new
  outer-loop UI without stalling.
- **Update campaign documentation for 10-level structure (AH-0MV39AQOY006I083)** —
  the campaign-structure documentation the outer loop will eventually supersede
  as the game's framing.
- **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience
  (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775)** — the validation lens the recommendation must survive.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No interactive interview round was run in this pass: the item was auto-dispatched
by the herdr downtime worker (comment `AH-C0MVNVFKO4004PPDH`) and no
ask-further-questions permission was recorded, so the requirements were clarified
from the item text, the GDD and the repo per the intake workflow's
no-questions path. The questions below are recorded with the assumption actually
adopted, so the producer can correct any of them without re-running intake.

- **Q1: Is the deliverable a design document, or does the item also expect the
  outer loop to be built?**
  — Adopted answer: **design document only.** Evidence: the item text ends "write
  an outline for each. I will choose one to be written up in the GDD", which
  places implementation and GDD specification after the producer's choice.
  Source: work-item description. Status: assumptive, correctable.
  **Recommended (had it been asked):** design-only — it matches the producer's
  stated sequence and keeps the item completable.

- **Q2: Where should the brainstorm live, and should it include the producer's
  own region proposal?**
  — Adopted answer: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, following the
  `docs/CLASSIC_*_RESEARCH.md` catalogue precedent, **including** the producer's
  proposal as Candidate A so the two alternatives are compared on equal footing.
  Evidence: GDD and README already reference the research catalogues; the item's
  proposal is recorded verbatim in the work item. Source: repo survey.
  **Recommended:** include Candidate A — comparing two alternatives against no
  baseline would make the recommendation untrustworthy.

- **Q3: Which two additional candidate directions should be explored?**
  — Adopted answer: **resource-persistent** (Salvage Fleet roguelite meta) and
  **knowledge-persistent** (Signal Decode campaign-mutating), because they differ
  from Candidate A's territorial axis in the thing that carries between runs
  (power/economy and information respectively), which makes the comparison
  meaningful rather than three re-skins of one idea. Evidence: Candidate A's axis
  is space/territory; nothing in the repo fixes an alternative. Source: repo and
  GDD survey. Status: assumptive, correctable — the producer may substitute
  directions.
  **Recommended:** these two — they span the three archetypal outer loops
  (territory, power, knowledge) that arcade-scale games actually use.

## Related work (automated report)

Produced by the `find-related` skill over the item's own text. The matches below
are keyword-level associations, not confirmed dependencies; the curated
*Related work* section above is the authoritative list.

### Related work items

- **Per-weapon level state on Player (AH-0MUQOTSFE00462EJ)** — completed; the
  per-weapon level store a persistent meta layer would have to seed (middle-loop
  state that an outer loop either extends or resets).
- **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)** — completed; precedent for
  exercising a gameplay element in a gym, which every candidate's *Gym
  testability* section depends on.
- **Power ups need to be larger (AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4)** — completed; keyword-level
  match only (power-up presentation), not a design dependency.

### Repository file matches

- `README.md` — matched: able, adjacent, another, around, attack (+63 more).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: able, adjacent, another, around,
  attack (+61 more).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: able, adjacent, another,
  around, attack (+57 more).

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-28 — Plan** (session herdr-1793151876-3167351-19031): pre-check `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk Medium — risk above the skip threshold). Duplicate-work search (`outer loop`, `OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES`, `home world region`, `salvage hangar roguelite`, `signal decode codex`) found no overlapping completed item. Decomposed into 3 children in test-first/dependency order: docs guard test + document skeleton (AH-0MVRNIWHG0099ZS3), candidate outlines + comparison + recommendation (AH-0MVRNJ0SL000RNHR), cross-links + docs + full-suite verification (AH-0MVRNJ6BB009IGZX). Dependency edges wired: content blocked by skeleton/guard; cross-link/verification blocked by content. AC coverage review: 100% (action proceed, 0 uncovered). Approval gate: no approval pause required (not Extra Large + High/Severe). Six automated review stages run. Design-only constraint preserved throughout: no gameplay, persistence-schema or scene implementation appears in any planned slice; the producer's choice and the GDD write-up remain a follow-on work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan, 2026-10-28)

No new producer questions were required for planning: the item's description already fixes the deliverable, the three candidates, the twelve-section outline, the comparison criteria, the ACs and the constraints, and the intake Appendix above records the three adoptable assumptions (design-only; `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` including Candidate A; Candidates B/C = resource-persistent and knowledge-persistent). Planning decisions taken without producer input are recorded here for correction:

- **Q4 (planning, agent decision, no producer input required): how should the deliverable be decomposed?** — Adopted: three linked work items — (1) docs guard test + document framing/skeleton/framing, (2) the three candidate outlines, comparison, recommendation, deferrals and decision record, (3) GDD §8 + README cross-links, docs updates and full-suite verification. Rationale: test-first ordering (the guard pins the structure before content), each slice is a green commit, and splitting the single document file into more slices would create avoidable worktree merge conflicts. **Recommended (had it been asked):** exactly this three-slice shape.
- **Q5 (planning, agent decision): should Candidate A be redesigned or preserved verbatim?** — Adopted: preserve every named mechanic as proposed (no redesign), per the item's "Recorded as proposed, not redesigned"; the slice must state Candidate A's minimal first slice. **Recommended:** preserve faithfully and state the minimal first slice.
- **No OPEN QUESTION blocks remain** for the planning phase. Any further producer decision is the candidate choice itself, which the document's pending "Producer decision record" reserves for the producer after the deliverable lands.

## Producer amendment (2026-10-29): Candidate D and the discovery-progression rules

The producer reviewed the delivered document and extended the brief. These
additions are **requirements**, not suggestions; they are implemented by child
work item **AH-0MVTE4EOS008RMQ7** (design-only, same deliverable).

- **Candidate A simplification.** The bot defence of a region and the accrual of
  minerals need not be complex: both may be an **algorithmic result** resolved
  from stored strength numbers rather than a live simulation. Candidate A's cost
  estimate and minimal first slice must reflect that reduction.
- **New Candidate D — Hangar War**, merging Candidate A and Candidate B, with
  **two outer-loop progressions**: (1) the war on the map (Candidate A) and
  (2) the increasing range of hulls / weapons / loadouts (Candidate B). The
  retained **hangar gains purpose** from the combination, and the goal becomes
  to **defend the hangar** rather than to find a world to live on.
  - The player starts **surrounded by AI on a hex grid**.
  - The player attacks a **weak** neighbouring hex, collects **salvage** and
    defeats the **boss**, gaining a **new kind of power-up or weapon** in the
    hangar.
  - The player **leaves a bot** in the captured hex, which attempts to
    **defend** it.
  - Over time the AI at the **borders get stronger** and can **retake previously
    won hexes**, unless the player goes to those neighbours and **defeats
    them**.
  - The map grows **in rings**, opening the door to future expansions.
  - **MVP = Candidate B's MVP plus one ring of hexes.**
- **Cross-cutting progression rules, all versions (A, B, C and D).**
  1. The player starts with a **reduced set of power-ups and upgrades**, so
     discovery and the collection of new experiences happen through play.
  2. **Mini-bosses introduce new upgrades and weapon types**: the player first
     has to **defeat a boss that uses it**, and only then gets to use it
     themselves.

**Extended acceptance criteria** (in addition to AC1–AC10 above, which continue
to apply to Candidates A–C):

11. **Candidate D is complete and faithful.** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
    carries `## Candidate D — Hangar War` with all twelve required sections,
    preserving every mechanic listed in this amendment (two progression axes,
    the hangar as the object to defend, the hex grid start surrounded by AI, the
    attack-weak-hex → salvage → boss → new-power-up cycle, the defending bot,
    strengthening borders that retake hexes unless the player defeats the
    neighbours, ring growth, and MVP = Candidate B's MVP + one ring).
12. **Cross-cutting progression rules are recorded and honoured.** A dedicated
    section states the reduced starting kit / discovery rule and the
    mini-boss-introduces-then-grants rule, and each of Candidates A–D states how
    it complies.
13. **Candidate A's algorithmic simplification is recorded.** Candidate A's
    *New systems required*, *Effort and risk* and *Minimal first slice* state
    that region defence and mineral accrual resolve algorithmically from stored
    strength numbers, with the reduced cost reflected in its sizing.
14. **The comparison, recommendation and decision record cover four
    candidates.** The comparison table ranks A–D across the eight criteria; the
    recommendation is explicit and ranked, placing D honestly against B (D is a
    superset of B's MVP); the producer decision record carries a pending
    Candidate D row.
15. **The docs guard covers the addition.** `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`
    asserts Candidate D's heading and twelve sections and the cross-cutting
    progression-rules section (headings and required terms only, never prose
    wording), and the full project test suite passes.

The GDD write-up of the chosen loop remains a **follow-on work item** after the
producer's decision; nothing in this amendment is scheduled or implemented.

## Producer-audit follow-through (2026-10-29T15:55, rgardler): AC16

The producer rejected this item at audit on 2026-10-29T15:55 with: *"Need a new AC
for this item that requires the producer to pick one and for that one to be
recorded in the GDD and a new work item created to built it out."* AC16 below
records that requirement. AC1–AC15 continue to apply unchanged.

16. **The choice is made, recorded and scheduled (producer pick, GDD record,
    build-out item).** This item is complete only once all three of the
    following hold:
    - **The producer picks one candidate** — one of Candidate A (Contested
      Regions / Home World), Candidate B (Salvage Fleet), Candidate C (Signal
      Decode) or Candidate D (Hangar War). This is a producer action; the agent
      must not pre-empt it (see AC8 and AC14, and the deliberately pending
      `## Producer decision record`).
    - **The pick is recorded in the GDD** — `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8
      states which loop was chosen (replacing the current "producer's choice left
      pending" wording, still without playable specification), and the
      `## Producer decision record` table in `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
      carries the decision, date and notes for the chosen candidate (the other
      rows stay `pending`/`not selected` with a reason).
    - **A new work item exists to build it out** — created with `wl create`
      (issue type `epic` or `feature`), named in a comment on this item and
      referenced from this description, so the chosen loop has a scheduled
      owner. It is a **linked** item (`discovered-from:AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC`),
      not a child, so this design item is not held open by the build-out.

    Until the producer's pick exists, this item stays out of `in_review` and
    carries `needsProducerReview` so the block is visible to the dispatcher.

### Status of AC16 at 2026-10-29 (implement run)

- **AC1–AC15: satisfied** — verified by the completed children
  AH-0MVRNIWHG0099ZS3, AH-0MVRNJ0SL000RNHR, AH-0MVRNJ6BB009IGZX and
  AH-0MVTE4EOS008RMQ7 (Candidate D + progression rules, commits on `dev` through

- **AC16: BLOCKED on producer input** — no candidate pick has been recorded in

# Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay objects as the main game

## Problem statement

Gym scenes are the canonical parity reference for the shipped game, yet the
level-launch gym path (`GymLevel`, which `GymBotTuning` extends) carries its own
inline wave-spawn implementation that has drifted from `PlayScene`. A designer
tuning the bot therefore watches enemies that do **not** behave as they do in
play, which invalidates the tuning signal the gym exists to provide.

## Findings from repo investigation (intake, 2026-10-27)

The reported symptom is real and is one of several divergences in the same spawn
seam:

1. **Phasers spawn in a line then snap to their ring (reported bug).**
   `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1647`) and
   `GymFormationScene` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1755`) both
   resolve an orbital entity's wormhole-transit destination through the entity's
   live `formationSlot()` seam (AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS). `GymLevel.spawnWave`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`) does not: its resolver returns the grid
   slot (`startX + driftX + col * spacingX`), so Phasers transit to a straight
   line and then snap onto the orbit when the spawn window ends. Because
   `GymBotTuning extends GymLevel` (`src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts:149`), the
   bot-tuning gym reproduces exactly the symptom the producer reported.
   Regression coverage exists for `PlayScene`
   (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6697`) and `GymFodderEnemies`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts:396`) but **not** for
   `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning`.

2. **Launched-level enemies never fire.** `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` assigns
   `entity.shootEnabled = spawn.shootEnabled`; `GymLevel.spawnWave` never
   assigns it, and `BaseEnemy._shootEnabled` defaults to `false`
   (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:97`), so every `tryFire*` method returns nothing.
   Campaign levels 4+ carry `shootEnabled: true`
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:157`), so a level launched from the curve editor or
   played in the bot-tuning gym is silently non-threatening. `GymLevel`'s own
   tests work around this by setting `victim.shootEnabled = true` by hand
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts:599`), which is itself evidence of the gap.

3. **March formations do not march.** `PlayScene` keeps a rigid `marchState`
   block and re-anchors march spawns (`_resetMarchFormation`,
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1737`); `GymLevel` has only horizontal `driftX`.
   Campaign levels 2–10 contain `march` groups
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:381-424`), so the launched block renders as a
   static line instead of the stepping/dropping block the game shows.

4. **The transit resolver is copied three times.** Each spawn site inlines the
   same non-trivial logic ("autonomous-mover exemption → orbital-slot branch →
   live slot / offset fallback"). The repo-wide duplicate-body guard
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`)
   does not cover this seam, which is why the third copy could drift unnoticed.
   `GymLevel` also keeps a legacy in-place spawn path used when no wormhole
   origin is supplied — dead for gameplay but still a second code path to keep
   honest.

5. **Divergences that must be preserved (already documented).** `GymPlayer`'s
   obstacle course, `GymWeapons`' AOE training targets, the flat supply cadence
   in `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, gym-only HUD/tuning panels and the
   absence of run telemetry are intentional and recorded in
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 and `docs/BALANCING.md`. The
   fix must not "unify" these away.

## Users and example user stories

- **Bot-tuning designer (primary):** "As a designer tuning the bot in
  `GymBotTuning`, I want the enemies I watch to spawn, transit, march and fire
  exactly as they do in the shipped game, so the tuning I save transfers to the
  attract demo and recordings."
- **Gameplay developer:** "As a developer landing a spawn/formation fix in
  `PlayScene`, I want the gyms to consume the same seam, so I cannot leave a gym
  behind without the test suite failing."
- **Level/curve designer:** "As a designer launching a campaign level from the
  curve editor, I want the launched level to be a faithful preview of the
  shipped level."

## Existing state

- Three spawn implementations: `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (game),
  `GymFormationScene` (formation gyms), `GymLevel.spawnWave` (level/bot-tuning
  gyms). Only the first two honour the `formationSlot` seam.
- Spawn presentation (`startSpawnAnimation`, wormhole open/close, spawn
  protection) is already shared via `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`; what diverges is
  the **destination resolver**, the per-enemy `shootEnabled` hand-off and the
  march block.
- Gym↔game parity coverage is extensive for combat, drops, movement, boss
  motion and projectile lifecycle, but has no coverage for the start-of-wave
  spawn presentation on the level-launch path.
- The capture/scripted-scene seam (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) is already
  consumed by `GymFormationScene` and `GymLevel` only, and the scene registry
  (`scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`) already lists every `Gym<Name>` as capturable
  except the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies`/`GymLevel`.

## Desired change

1. Extract the wormhole-transit destination resolution into **one** shared
   helper under `src/scenes/core/` and make all four spawn sites
   (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss` minions) consume it,
   so the orbital-slot seam, the autonomous-mover exemption and the live-slot
   tracking can no longer drift.
2. Propagate the wave's per-enemy `shootEnabled` (and the formation RNG) through
   the `GymLevel` spawn path exactly as `PlayScene` does.
3. Bring the march block to the level-launch path (or consume the shared march
   state) so launched march waves step and drop as they do in the game.
4. Register the new seam in the duplicate-body guard and add cross-scene
   equivalence tests that boot `PlayScene` and `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` with the
   same seeded orbital/march wave and assert identical spawn trajectories and
   identical fire cadence.
5. Sweep **every** gym scene (`src/scenes/gym/`, including the generic
   `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path) against `PlayScene` for
   enabled-object parity and record the result in a single parity matrix. **Fix
   every real divergence found in this item** (each with a test), rather than
   deferring them; documented, intentional divergences stay, with their reason
   recorded in the matrix.
6. Adopt the scripted-scene `setup` seam in **every** gym in this item: each gym
   applies the shared `applySceneSetup` applier and exposes whatever
   scene-specific scenario parameters it needs (enemy roster, formation, level,
   toggles) through the capture scene config, so any gym can be driven from
   `examples/scenes.json` and recorded. Extend the config validation and the
   `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` / parameterised-scene contracts accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel` (and therefore `GymBotTuning`) with the same seeded orbital wave produces the same per-frame transit target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the entity's live `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is ever placed on a straight line then snapped to the ring. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after).
- [ ] AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel` / `GymBotTuning` at the same cadence and bullet speed as the same wave in `PlayScene` (shared dispatcher, real scene clock). Verified by a parity test, not a hand-set `shootEnabled` in the test.
- [ ] AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps/drops in the gym exactly as the game's block does for the same `dt` sequence. Verified by a parity test.
- [ ] AC4 — The spawn-transit destination logic is defined exactly **once** repo-wide, is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`, and every spawn site (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss`) resolves to it; the duplicate-body guard fails if a copy is re-introduced.
- [ ] AC5 — A gym↔game parity matrix document records, for **every** gym scene under `src/scenes/gym/` (including the generic `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path), which shipped gameplay objects it runs, whether it inherits the shipped start-of-wave/combat code, and — where it diverges — the reason. Every real divergence identified by the sweep is **fixed in this item** with a regression test; retained divergences are only those already documented as intentional and each is re-justified in the matrix.
- [ ] AC6 — Every gym applies the shared scripted-scene `setup` seam and exposes its scenario parameters through the capture scene config, so any gym can be launched and recorded from `examples/scenes.json`; the scene-config validator rejects unsupported/parameterised targets with a clear error, and the `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` registry contract and its pinning test are updated.
- [ ] AC7 — `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (and `AGENTS.md` § Game Architecture Conventions where the rule text changes) explain the shared spawn seam and point at the parity matrix; the docs guard test still passes.
- [ ] AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (including the scripted-scene/gym capture documentation).
- [ ] AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No balance changes. Behavioural differences introduced by this item must be a
  *fix toward* the game's behaviour, except where the producer explicitly asks
  for a new gym capability (scripted-scene setup, AC6).
- Must not "fix" documented intentional divergences (obstacle course, AOE
  practice targets, flat formation-gym supply cadence, gym HUD); each must keep
  its documented reason.
- Must not regress the automation that consumes the gyms: the capture CLI and
  `sceneSetup` appliers, Watch Demo / demo mode, the bot-tuning store, and the
  `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` registry contract.
- Scope is deliberately broad (producer direction: sweep and fix all in this
  item). If the sweep uncovers a divergence that cannot be fixed without a
  separate design decision, record it as a blocker with evidence on this item
  rather than silently expanding the design.
- The item is expected to be decomposed into child items at the plan stage
  (shared seam, spawn-parity fixes, gym sweep, scripted-scene adoption, docs);
  the ACs above are the whole-item contract.
- The reported symptom must be reproducible before the fix and demonstrably
  fixed after it (red-before / green-after per repo convention).
- Implementation runs in the item's own worktree per `AGENTS.md`.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` — **new** shared destination-resolver seam
  (orbital slot / offset fallback / autonomous exemption / live-slot tracking).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — consume the shared seam from `_spawnEnemy`;
  keep march state as the single source for block anchoring.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — replace its inline resolver.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — consume the seam, propagate `shootEnabled` and
  the formation RNG, adopt the march block or document why not.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — inherits the fix; update its divergence
  note if the scenario description changes.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — minion spawn keeps the in-place (no-transit)
  behaviour through the same seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — register the new helper
  in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`; add cross-scene spawn equivalence coverage.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts` — spawn/fire/march parity assertions.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§5.1) and a new gym parity matrix
  document (e.g. `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`) listing every gym scene, the shipped
  objects it runs and its divergences.
- `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — docs guard update if the rule text
  changes.
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` — extend the applier so every gym can take a
  setup; `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` and its tests — extend the config schema,
  parameterised-target handling and `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` contract.
- `src/scenes/gym/*.ts` (all 14 gym scenes, including `GymCurveSequencer`,
  `GymPlayer`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUps*`, `GymWeaponLeveling`,
  `GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymMinerals`, `GymCentipede`, `GymMiniBoss`) — apply the
  setup seam and fix any divergence the sweep finds.
- `examples/scenes.json` and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — demonstrate a
  scripted scene for each gym family.

## Related work

- Wormhole/transit/formation-slot lineage: AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW (enemies emerge
  from the wormhole), AH-0MVDW3T9R0054HG6 (transit movement, parity, docs),
  AH-0MVDW3R7300979DC (scene-level transit tests), AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS (Phasers
  spawn in a line then snap), AH-0MVF4P31M0033RAC (shared orbital geometry and
  orbital transit destination), AH-0MVF4OVY6000DZE8 (orbital geometry tests),
  AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC (wormhole placement), AH-0MV9KHLV8006GMX6 (wormhole
  lifecycle).
- Gym parity principle and guards: AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 (docs the parity
  principle), AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P / AH-0MVLJF6ZD00164MG (level gym scaling
  parity), AH-0MV9AWR7A0084XJ0 (bot-tuning gym scenario parity gap — same class
  of defect, already completed).
- Scripted-scene / capture lineage: AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB (scripted scenes for
  video, open, needs producer review), AH-0MVNW8VNN004FFK1 (shared scene-setup
  applier), AH-0MVNW90FB003H3KM (setup determinism seed), AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX
  (generated-level scenes), AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL (Watch Demo flies saved
  bot-tuning).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (blocking) — implementation shape.** "Should the fix land as one shared
  spawn-transit seam consumed by `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`
  and `GymBoss`, or as a minimal local patch to `GymLevel.spawnWave`? Options:
  (a) extract a shared seam in `src/scenes/core/`, consume it at all four spawn
  sites, register it in the duplicate-body guard, and add cross-scene spawn
  equivalence tests; (b) minimal patch — add the `formationSlot` branch and the
  `shootEnabled` hand-off to `GymLevel.spawnWave` only, with tests, leaving the
  three copies in place; (c) other. **Recommended: (a)** — this is the third
  divergent copy of the same resolver and the guard did not catch it, so a local
  patch leaves the next drift unguarded." — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-27): "A"**
  ⇒ option (a): one shared spawn-transit seam in `src/scenes/core/`, consumed
  by all four spawn sites, registered in the duplicate-body guard, with
  cross-scene spawn equivalence tests. Source: interactive producer reply on the
  resume prompt.
- **Q2 (blocking) — audit depth and deliverable.** "How far should 'check all
  others too' go? Options: (a) sweep every gym scene against `PlayScene` for
  start-of-wave/spawn and enabled-object parity, publish a parity matrix, fix the
  real divergences found in this item and file child items for anything that
  should not be fixed now; (b) fix only the spawn-path divergences named in this
  brief (Phaser orbit, `shootEnabled`, march) with a test per gym, no matrix;
  (c) sweep and fix every divergence found, however large, before closing.
  **Recommended: (a)** — bounded, auditable, and it prevents an open-ended
  fix-everything scope while still honouring the request to check all gyms."
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-27): "A sweep and fix"** ⇒ interpreted as (a)'s
  sweep + parity matrix **plus** (c)'s fix-in-this-item, consistent with the Q3
  answer "fix all in this item": every gym is swept against `PlayScene`, the
  matrix is published, and every real divergence found is fixed here rather than
  deferred to child items. Recorded as a documented assumption; if the producer
  meant "sweep + defer some fixes" that is a plan-stage adjustment, not a change
  of intent. Source: interactive producer reply.
- **Q3 (blocking) — scripted-scene adoption.** "Should this item also configure
  every gym to run under the scripted-scene `setup` seam? Options: (a) track it
  separately — this item stays a parity fix and a follow-up child item extends
  `applySceneSetup` to every gym and makes gym scenarios expressible in
  `examples/scenes.json`; (b) include it here — extend the setup applier to all
  gyms (including roster/formation/toggle fields, since `GymFodderEnemies` and
  `GymLevel` are parameterised) and make every gym capturable from config;
  (c) document only — describe how gyms can be scripted, no code. **Recommended:
  (a)** — the parity fix is already large and the setup extension depends on it;
  keeping the capture work in its own item preserves reviewable, testable
  scope." — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-27): "fix all in this item"** ⇒ option
  (b): the scripted-scene `setup` adoption for every gym is in scope for this
  item (AC6), not deferred. Source: interactive producer reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ** – Gym index scene (completed)
- **AH-0MVFC6TCY005E39P** – Pure scene-capture module: config parsing, validation and timing (completed)
- **AH-0MVKXBZ5N007LKH4** – Implement: wrap seams wired into PlayScene and gyms (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv6mfdyg001e6pl, 0mve01ey0008qevx, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, ac1, ac2 (+424 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvexvme1004siis, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+416 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, 0mv8br9y70079tkc, 0mv8bsmxc0097klw, 0mv9awr7a0084xj0, 0mv9khlv8006gmx6 (+410 more)

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-28)

Decomposed into 9 child items in **test-first, dependency order**. Each child is a vertical slice
(code + tests + docs for its layer) and restates the parent AC(s) it owns under a
`## Parent AC coverage (traceability)` section.

| # | Child | Type | Priority | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|----------|------------|
| 1 | Test: cross-scene spawn/fire/march parity for the level-launch path (red-before) (AH-0MVRMHJZS001Z6CX) | task | high | — |
| 2 | Shared wormhole-transit destination seam consumed by all four spawn sites (AH-0MVRMHQC9003VDNN) | task | high | 1 |
| 3 | GymLevel / GymBotTuning spawn parity: orbital transit, shootEnabled, march (AH-0MVRMHSKH0066J9B) | bug | high | 2 |
| 4 | Gym↔game parity sweep of all 14 gym scenes and published parity matrix (AH-0MVRMHUOG005P38A) | task | medium | 3 |
| 5 | Fix every real gym-game divergence found by the parity sweep (AH-0MVRMHWNC002H4B5) | bug | medium | 4 |
| 6 | Scripted-scene setup adoption in every gym scene (AH-0MVRMHYJR000Y9H8) | feature | medium | 3 |
| 7 | Capture config schema, validator and registry for gym scenario parameters (AH-0MVRMI0Q7001KG4Y) | feature | medium | 6 |
| 8 | Docs: parity rule text, §5.1 spawn seam, matrix links and capture guide (AH-0MVRMI2M50098WN5) | docs | medium | 5, 7 |
| 9 | Validate: typecheck, build, full suite and parity guards (AH-0MVRMI4K700048OB) | task | medium | 8 |

**Slice 1 — red-before evidence (1 → 2 → 3).** Tests first, then a behaviour-preserving seam
extraction, then the behaviour fix that flips the red tests green. This keeps "the reported symptom
is reproducible before the fix and demonstrably fixed after it" verifiable at every step, and keeps
the refactor reviewable apart from the behaviour change.

**Slice 2 — sweep and fix (4 → 5).** The matrix is authored by 4 (audit + guard + classification)
and the fix scope is exactly the rows 4 marks `divergence to fix`, consumed by 5. Splitting them
keeps the audit honest (no fixing while auditing) while still honouring the producer's
"fix all in this item" direction: nothing is deferred to a new item; a divergence needing a
separate design decision is recorded as a blocker on this parent with evidence.

**Slice 3 — scripted-scene adoption (6 → 7).** In-scene capability (every gym applies
`applySceneSetup` and exposes scenario parameters) precedes the config/validator/registry contract
that declares those parameters, so the schema cannot describe fields the scenes do not support.

**Slice 4 — documentation and gate (8, 9).** Docs describe the final state, then one recorded
validation pass.

**Vertical-slice check:** every child touches its own tests and the docs/comments for what it
changes; no child is a pure horizontal layer. Between phases the next child's description is
reviewed and updated (dependency edges already encode the ordering).

**Approval gate:** `plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate` returned `request_approval: false`
(effort Large, risk High — below the Extra-Large + High threshold), so no producer approval pause
was taken; the six automated review stages ran instead.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 — plan skill: created 9 child features (AH-0MVRMHJZS001Z6CX, AH-0MVRMHQC9003VDNN,
  AH-0MVRMHSKH0066J9B, AH-0MVRMHUOG005P38A, AH-0MVRMHWNC002H4B5, AH-0MVRMHYJR000Y9H8,
  AH-0MVRMI0Q7001KG4Y, AH-0MVRMI2M50098WN5, AH-0MVRMI4K700048OB); wired test-first dependency edges;
  added `## Parent AC coverage` traceability to each child; ran the six automated review stages and
  the AC coverage review (100% parent-AC coverage, stage → `plan_complete`); reformatted the
  acceptance-criteria block to one bullet per AC so tooling extracts full criteria; refreshed the
  effort/risk estimate against the child WBS (Large / High, ≈66 h expected, 87 h recommended).

## Appendix — plan-stage entries

- **Q4 (no new questions asked).** All three blocking questions (Q1 shared seam, Q2 sweep-and-fix,
  Q3 scripted-scene adoption) were answered at intake and the answers already fix the shape of the
  work, so no further question was raised at plan stage. **Final: no new questions.** Evidence: the
  Q1–Q3 answers above.
- **Assumption (recorded, non-blocking).** Q2's answer ("A sweep and fix") is read as *sweep and
  publish the matrix **and** fix every real divergence in this item* (not defer to child items),
  consistent with the Q3 answer "fix all in this item". Consequently the fix scope is not
  enumerated up front — it is defined by the sweep (AH-0MVRMHUOG005P38A) and executed by
  AH-0MVRMHWNC002H4B5, whose acceptance criterion is "zero rows left marked `divergence to fix`".
- **Assumption (recorded, non-blocking).** "Every gym" means every scene under `src/scenes/gym/`
  (14 scenes) plus the generic base `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` as an audited row;
  `PlayScene` remains the reference and is never changed to match a gym.
- **OPEN QUESTION (producer, non-blocking — resolvable inside AH-0MVRMI0Q7001KG4Y).**
  `GymCurveSequencer` extends `Phaser.Scene` directly (it is the curve-editor UI, not a combat
  scene, and is already in `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS`). Should its curve-editor scenario (the edited
  curve, the launched level) be expressible in `examples/scenes.json`, or is it documented as an
  intentional exclusion with a reason? Why it matters: it decides whether the capture schema grows a
  curve/level parameter family or records an exclusion. Default resolution if the producer does not
  answer: apply `applySceneSetup`/seed where meaningful, expose the launched level as the scenario
  parameter, and document any unreachable editor state as an intentional exclusion in
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`. Not blocking: the child's AC4 requires the
  decision (and its reason) to be recorded either way.

# Shared wormhole-transit destination seam, consumed by all four spawn sites

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC4, and prerequisite for AC1). **Pure refactor: behaviour must not
change in any scene.**

## Goal / user story

As a gameplay developer, I want the wormhole-transit destination resolution defined exactly once,
so that the game and every gym consume the same "autonomous-mover exemption → orbital live slot →
grid-slot/offset fallback" rule, and a re-introduced copy fails the suite.

## Problem

The resolver is currently inlined three times:

- `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1647`) — the reference behaviour
  (`formationSlot` seam + `marchState` base + `driftX`).
- `GymFormationScene._spawnFormation` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1755`) — same
  rule, portal-based base, no march.
- `GymLevel.spawnWave` (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`) — a **divergent** copy that returns the
  grid slot and therefore reproduces the reported "Phaser spawns in a line then snaps" symptom.
- `GymBoss` minion spawn (`src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts:274`) — no resolver at all (in-place).

The repo-wide duplicate-body guard (`EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) does not cover this seam, which is why the third
copy could drift unnoticed.

## Desired change

1. New module `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` exporting **one** resolver, e.g.
   `resolveSpawnTransitTarget(...)`, which takes the narrow structural inputs it needs and returns
   `{ x, y }` or `undefined` (meaning "no transit — spawn in place"):
   - the entity (read structurally for `autonomousPositioning` and optional `formationSlot`);
   - the base position for this frame (march base when the wave is a march block, else
     `startX + driftX`, `startY`);
   - the formation `offset` and the group `spacingX` / `spacingY`.
   The resolver owns the rule only — it must not import Phaser, must not read scene fields, and must
   not mutate the entity.
2. Consume it at **all four** spawn sites. Each site keeps its own *base* computation (the game's
   `marchState`, the formation gym's portal, the level gym's launched drift, the boss's in-place
   exemption) — that is scene structure, not the rule.
3. `GymLevel` consumes the seam with **unchanged** behaviour in this item (it will still pass its
   grid-slot base, because it has no march/formation-slot wiring yet); the behaviour fix lands in
   the follow-up `GymLevel` parity item. This keeps this item a verifiable no-op refactor.
4. Register the resolver in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` with the canonical definer path, and extend the
   guard fixture so a re-introduced copy is proven to fail (the guard already has a
   "detects a re-introduced duplicate" describe block to extend).

## Implementation guidance

- Keep the ordering of the existing rule exactly: **autonomous → orbital live slot → grid offset**.
  The orbital branch must call `formationSlot.call(entity, baseX, baseY)` so the entity's own
  geometry stays authoritative (AH-0MVF4P31M0033RAC, AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS).
- Preserve every existing comment's intent by moving the rationale into the new module's header
  (the "never appear in a line then snap onto the ring" reason) and leaving short pointers at the
  four call sites.
- Prefer a structural input type over importing entity classes, so the module stays pure and the
  gyms can pass their own shapes.
- Do not "fix" the `GymLevel` behaviour here; the red-before tests from the parity-test item must
  still fail after this item lands.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` exists, is Phaser-free (importable in a node-only
  unit test), and defines the transit destination rule exactly once.
- [ ] AC2 — `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and `GymBoss` all resolve their transit
  destination through that single helper; no site re-implements the orbital/autonomous/offset
  branch chain.
- [ ] AC3 — The helper is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, the single-definer guard passes, and the
  guard's duplicate-detection fixture covers the new helper.
- [ ] AC4 — Unit tests for the new helper cover: autonomous mover → `undefined`; orbital entity →
  live `formationSlot` result (including a slot that differs from the grid slot); non-orbital
  entity → grid slot from base + offset × spacing; march base vs drift base input handling.
- [ ] AC5 — Every pre-existing test passes unchanged (no behaviour change): scene behaviour is
  identical before and after the refactor, verified by the existing PlayScene, GymFormationScene,
  GymBoss and GymLevel suites plus the equivalence suite.
- [ ] AC6 — The red-before parity tests added by AH-0MVRMHJZS001Z6CX still fail after this item
  (proving the refactor alone does not "fix" the bug).

- AC4 — The spawn-transit destination logic is defined exactly **once** repo-wide, is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`, and every spawn site (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss`) resolves to it; the duplicate-body guard fails if a copy is re-introduced. — **contribution:** this item delivers it in full (see Parent AC coverage below).

## Key files

- `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` (new) and `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_spawnEnemy`)
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (`_spawnFormation`)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` (`spawnWave`)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` (minion spawn)
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (`EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` + guard fixture)

## Constraints

- No behaviour change in any scene; this item is reviewed as a refactor.
- No balance change.
- Must not touch the documented intentional divergences (obstacle course, AOE targets, flat
  formation-gym supply cadence, gym HUD, no telemetry).

## Parent AC coverage (traceability)

This child contributes to parent AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV. The seam extraction guarantees the single-definition requirement of this AC across all four spawn sites.

Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim from the parent brief):

- **Parent AC4 — The spawn-transit destination logic is defined exactly **once** repo-wide, is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`, and every spawn site (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss`) resolves to it; the duplicate-body guard fails if a copy is re-introduced.**

# GymLevel / GymBotTuning spawn parity: orbital transit, shootEnabled, march

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC1, AC2, AC3). This is the **behaviour fix** that turns the
red-before parity tests green.

## Goal / user story

As a designer tuning the bot in `GymBotTuning`, I want the enemies I watch to spawn, transit, march
and fire exactly as they do in the shipped game, so the tuning I save transfers to the attract demo
and to recordings.

## Problem (three divergences in one seam)

1. **Phasers spawn in a line then snap to their ring.** `GymLevel.spawnWave` (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`)
   resolves the transit destination as the grid slot (`startX + driftX + col*spacingX`), while
   `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` and `GymFormationScene` resolve it through the entity's live
   `formationSlot()`. Because `GymBotTuning extends GymLevel`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts:149`), the reported symptom reproduces there.
2. **Launched-level enemies never fire.** `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` assigns
   `entity.shootEnabled = spawn.shootEnabled`; `GymLevel.spawnWave` never assigns it, and
   `BaseEnemy._shootEnabled` defaults to `false` (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:97`), so every
   `tryFire*` returns nothing. Campaign levels 4+ carry `shootEnabled: true`
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:157`), so a launched level or bot-tuning run is silently
   non-threatening. `GymLevel.test.ts:~599` works around this by setting `shootEnabled` by hand.
3. **March formations do not march.** `PlayScene` keeps a rigid `marchState` block and re-anchors
   march spawns (`_resetMarchFormation`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1737`); `GymLevel` has only
   horizontal `driftX`. Campaign levels 2–10 contain `march` groups
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:381-424`), so a launched block renders as a static line.

## Desired change

1. **Orbital destination.** Feed the shared `resolveSpawnTransitTarget` seam
   (`src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts`, from AH-0MVRMHQC9003VDNN) the correct per-frame base so
   an orbital entity's transit target is its live formation slot, not the grid line. Do **not**
   keep a second branch in `GymLevel`.
2. **shootEnabled + formation RNG.** Propagate `group.shootEnabled` onto each spawned entity exactly
   as `PlayScene` does, and thread the formation RNG (`createEnemyFromConfig`'s rng argument) the
   same way the game does, so per-enemy randomness in the gym is the game's randomness. Remove
   reliance on hand-set `shootEnabled` in `GymLevel.test.ts` and assert the hand-off instead.
3. **March block.** Adopt the shared march module (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts` —
   `createMarchState`, `computeMarchBounds`, `advanceMarch`, `marchSpeedMultiplier`, already
   consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`) on the level-launch path so a launched march
   wave steps, reverses and drops as the game's block does, and march spawns re-anchor to the block
   base during transit. Do not copy `PlayScene`'s block-mutation code — if `PlayScene`'s march
   bookkeeping is itself scene-specific, extract only what is genuinely shared and document the
   remainder; a second march implementation is not acceptable.
4. Keep the launched-level preview honest: the gym must not regress its existing level scaling /
   supply-cadence parity (AH-0MVLJF6ZD00164MG) or the force-field resolution at the launched level
   (AH-0MVM8GXEF009883O).

## Implementation guidance

- Prefer a small `GymLevel`-local march holder that owns `MarchState` + `MarchOptions` for the
  active wave, mirroring `PlayScene._resetMarchFormation` / its per-tick advance, but call the
  shared pure `advanceMarch` — the policy stays shared, only the holder differs. If the holder
  logic is identical to `PlayScene`'s, extract that holder (a class or factory) into
  `src/scenes/core/` and register it in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` rather than duplicating it.
- `GymLevel` spawns a whole `WaveDefinition` per launch and re-spawns on level launch; reset the
  march state exactly where `PlayScene` resets it (per wave), not per enemy.
- `GymBotTuning` inherits the fix; only its divergence note (if it describes the scenario) needs
  updating.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` with the same seeded orbital wave
  produces the same per-frame transit target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the
  entity's live `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is placed on a straight line then snapped to the
  ring. The red-before test from AH-0MVRMHJZS001Z6CX is flipped to green by this item.
- [ ] AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` at the same
  cadence and bullet speed as in `PlayScene` through the shared dispatcher (`fireForEnemy`), with
  the flag flowing from the wave definition — the hand-set `shootEnabled` in `GymLevel.test.ts` is
  deleted and a test asserts the hand-off from the wave/spawn descriptor.
- [ ] AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps, reverses and drops identically to the game's block for
  the same `dt` sequence (parity test green).
- [ ] AC4 — `GymLevel`'s transit destination contains no orbital/autonomous branch of its own — it
  resolves through the shared seam (statically asserted by the duplicate-body guard).
- [ ] AC5 — Existing level-gym parity is preserved: `levelParity.test.ts` (scaled counts, supply
  cadence) and the force-field tests still pass, and a manual/scripted check of a launched
  campaign level shows firing and marching enemies.
- [ ] AC6 — No balance change: the fix makes gym behaviour match the game, and the game's behaviour
  is unchanged (verified by the untouched `PlayScene` suite).

- AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel` (and therefore `GymBotTuning`) with the same seeded orbital wave produces the same per-frame transit target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the entity's live `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is ever placed on a straight line then snapped to the ring. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after). — **contribution:** this item delivers the behaviour-fix half that makes the test green (see Parent AC coverage below).

- AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel` / `GymBotTuning` at the same cadence and bullet speed as the same wave in `PlayScene` (shared dispatcher, real scene clock). Verified by a parity test, not a hand-set `shootEnabled` in the test. — **contribution:** this item delivers the shootEnabled hand-off that makes the test green (see Parent AC coverage below).

- AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps/drops in the gym exactly as the game's block does for the same `dt` sequence. Verified by a parity test. — **contribution:** this item delivers the march adoption that makes the test green (see Parent AC coverage below).

## Key files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` (`spawnWave`, march holder, per-tick update)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` (divergence note only)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts` (remove the hand-set `shootEnabled` workaround)
- `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts` / new `spawnParity.test.ts` (flip red→green)
- `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts`, `src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts` (consume)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (reference behaviour only — must not change)
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` (`shootEnabled`, `march` groups)

## Constraints

- Behaviour changes must be *toward* the game; never change `PlayScene` to match the gym.
- Do not regress the capture CLI, Watch Demo / demo mode, the bot-tuning store, or the
  `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` contract.

## Parent AC coverage (traceability)

This child contributes to parent AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV. This item is the behaviour fix that flips the red-before parity tests from AH-0MVRMHJZS001Z6CX to green.

Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim from the parent brief):

- **Parent AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel` (and therefore `GymBotTuning`) with the same seeded orbital wave produces the same per-frame transit target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the entity's live `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is ever placed on a straight line then snapped to the ring. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after).**

- **Parent AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel` / `GymBotTuning` at the same cadence and bullet speed as the same wave in `PlayScene` (shared dispatcher, real scene clock). Verified by a parity test, not a hand-set `shootEnabled` in the test.**

- **Parent AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps/drops in the gym exactly as the game's block does for the same `dt` sequence. Verified by a parity test.**

# Gym↔game parity sweep of all 14 gym scenes and published parity matrix

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC5, first half).

## Goal / user story

As a gameplay developer, I want a single published matrix that records, for every gym scene, which
shipped gameplay objects it runs, whether it inherits the shipped start-of-wave/combat code, and
where it diverges and why — so the parity claim is auditable instead of assumed.

## Scope — every gym must appear

All scenes under `src/scenes/gym/` (14, including the generic base and the level/bot-tuning path):

`GymBoss`, `GymBotTuning`, `GymCentipede`, `GymCurveSequencer`, `GymFodderEnemies`, `GymLevel`,
`GymMinerals`, `GymMiniBoss`, `GymPlayer`, `GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`,
`GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeaponLeveling`, `GymWeapons`
— plus the generic base `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` as its own row.

## What the sweep must check, per gym

1. **Enabled gameplay objects** — which entities, weapons, power-ups, drops, minerals and hazards
   are live, and whether each runs the shipped code (shared core / shared helper / shared entity)
   or a gym-local implementation.
2. **Start-of-wave / spawn path** — which spawn seam the gym uses (shared core template, shared
   `spawnTransit` seam, `GymLevel.spawnWave`, in-place), whether wormhole presentation is the
   shared one, and whether transit destination/`shootEnabled`/march are honoured.
3. **Combat inheritance** — whether the gym derives from `CombatScene` / `CombatCoreScene` /
   `GymFormationScene` (and therefore inherits the shipped update/collision/fire/drop loops) or
   runs its own loop.
4. **Divergences** — every intentional divergence with its documented reason and the file/section
   that records it. Expected intentional divergences to re-justify (do not "fix" them):
   `GymPlayer`'s obstacle course, `GymWeapons`' AOE `TrainingTarget`s, the flat supply cadence in
   `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, gym-only HUD/tuning panels, and the absence of run telemetry.
5. **Classification** — each row gets a verdict: `parity`, `intentional divergence (reason)`, or
   `divergence to fix`. Anything marked `divergence to fix` is handed to the sibling fix item; every
   row must end up `parity` or `intentional divergence`.

## Deliverable

A new `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` containing:

- A table with one row per gym scene: scene | derives from | enabled shipped objects | spawn seam |
  combat loop inherited | verdict | reason / evidence (file:line).
- A short "how to re-audit" section saying which seams are guarded automatically
  (`EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` / `EPIC_SHARED_METHODS`, `gymParityDocs.test.ts`) and which are
  human-reviewed, so the next sweep is cheap.
- An explicit statement that `PlayScene` is the reference and that the game must never be changed to
  match a gym.

Add a docs guard (extend `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` or a sibling test) that fails if a
gym scene exists under `src/scenes/gym/` without a row in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, so the matrix cannot
rot as gyms are added.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records every gym scene under `src/scenes/gym/` (14 scenes plus the
  generic `GymFormationScene` row), with enabled shipped objects, spawn seam, combat-loop
  inheritance and verdict per row.
- [ ] AC2 — Every divergence is classified `intentional divergence (<reason + evidence>)` or
  `divergence to fix`; all five known intentional divergences are re-justified with a file/section
  reference and no intentional divergence is "fixed" by this item.
- [ ] AC3 — An automated guard fails if a `Gym*.ts` production scene under `src/scenes/gym/` has no
  row in the matrix (red-before demonstrated by adding a temporary scene or by asserting against a
  fixture, then green).
- [ ] AC4 — Every `divergence to fix` row is recorded with enough evidence (file:line, observed vs
  expected, reproduction steps) for the sibling fix item to act on without re-auditing.
- [ ] AC5 — The audit itself introduces no behaviour change: production code is untouched apart from
  the docs guard test; the suite stays green.
- [ ] AC6 — The sweep explicitly reports on the three known spawn divergences (orbital transit,
  `shootEnabled`, march) as fixed-by-sibling or still-open, so the matrix agrees with the fix item.

- AC5 — A gym↔game parity matrix document records, for **every** gym scene under `src/scenes/gym/` (including the generic `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path), which shipped gameplay objects it runs, whether it inherits the shipped start-of-wave/combat code, and — where it diverges — the reason. Every real divergence identified by the sweep is **fixed in this item** with a regression test; retained divergences are only those already documented as intentional and each is re-justified in the matrix. — **contribution:** this item delivers the sweep and matrix half (see Parent AC coverage below).

## Key files

- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (new)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (cross-reference; full text update is the docs item)
- `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` (extend guard) — or a new sibling guard test
- `src/scenes/gym/*.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (audit targets, read-only)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` (intentional-divergence references)

## Constraints

- Audit-and-document item: do not fix divergences here (that is the sibling fix item), except where
  a gap is purely a missing matrix row.
- Do not weaken existing guards or docs assertions.

## Parent AC coverage (traceability)

This child contributes to parent AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV. This item owns the sweep and the matrix; the sibling fix item (AH-0MVRMHWNC002H4B5) owns the fixes the matrix schedules.

Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim from the parent brief):

- **Parent AC5 — A gym↔game parity matrix document records, for **every** gym scene under `src/scenes/gym/` (including the generic `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path), which shipped gameplay objects it runs, whether it inherits the shipped start-of-wave/combat code, and — where it diverges — the reason. Every real divergence identified by the sweep is **fixed in this item** with a regression test; retained divergences are only those already documented as intentional and each is re-justified in the matrix.**
